inlineContent.text: Base class for any object that keeps a reference count.
and many other helper objects inherit this class.

s therefore do not need to be freed manually with
instances caught in a cyclic reference will
be freed automatically. For example, if a node holds a reference to instance
, which directly or indirectly holds a reference back to
’s reference count will be 2. Destruction of the node will leave
dangling with a reference count of 1, and there will be a memory leak. To prevent this, one of the references in the cycle can be made weak with
In the vast majority of use cases, instantiating and using
-derived types is all you need to do. The methods provided in this class are only for advanced users, and can cause issues if misused.

In C#, reference-counted objects will not be freed instantly after they are no longer in use. Instead, garbage collection will run periodically and will free reference-counted objects that are no longer in use. This means that unused ones will remain in memory for a while before being removed.
